query: Why don't people need to show their ID to vote?
official_answer: Maryland Election Law does not require the presentation of ID when voting. This is a policy decision made by the General Assembly. There are proposals presented to the General Assembly each year. If you wish for this type of process to be adopted, you should contact your State Senator and House of Delegate members.
model_response:
In Maryland, you generally don’t need to show ID to vote. ID is only required in certain situations:

- You’re voting for the first time in Maryland and you didn’t previously meet the ID requirements. You must provide ID to the local board before 10 am on the 2nd Wednesday after election day; acceptable forms include a Maryland driver’s license/MVA ID, U.S. passport, or a recent document showing your name and address (dated within 3 months) [Provisional Voting](https://elections.maryland.gov/voting/provisional_voting.html).

- You registered to vote or changed your address during early voting and you didn’t prove where you live. You must provide proof of residency (same ID options listed above) by the same deadline (10 am on the 2nd Wednesday after election day) [Provisional Voting](https://elections.maryland.gov/voting/provisional_voting.html).

- You vote provisionally. Provisional ballots are counted if you meet all eligibility requirements, but you may be asked to show ID to verify your eligibility [Provisional Voting](https://elections.maryland.gov/voting/provisional_voting.html).

So, for most voters in regular situations, ID isn’t required; it’s only needed in these specific cases.
